0cc2c1f982e8.en: Here are the most common words in the thirty novels, counted twice. <bookmark mark='a'/> On the left, Part 17's program, which kept every distinct word in a hash table. On the right, this part's program. The counts agree, all twenty words and all twenty numbers. <bookmark mark='b'/> But the first program needed almost two megabytes, and the second needs eighteen and a half kilobytes, a hundred times less. <bookmark mark='c'/> The second program doesn't store the words it counts at all, apart from a few dozen candidates. It does it by flipping coins, and it is exactly right only with high probability. By the end of this part we will know how high.
0cc2c1f982e8.zh: 这是三十部小说中最常见的词，数了两遍。<bookmark mark='a'/>左边是第17部分的程序，它把每个不同的词都存进一张哈希表。右边是这一部分的程序。两边的计数一致，二十个词、二十个数都一样。<bookmark mark='b'/>但第一个程序需要将近两兆字节，第二个只要十八点五千字节，少了一百倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>第二个程序根本不存储它所统计的词，只留几十个候选。它靠抛硬币做到这一点，而且只是以很高的概率完全正确。到这一部分结束时，我们会知道这个概率有多高。

625e7b6235f3.en: That is the theme of this part: a coin flip can stand in for cleverness. <bookmark mark='a'/> With coins we can check a claimed matrix product in n squared time instead of recomputing it. <bookmark mark='b'/> We can find the weakest link of a network by contracting random edges. <bookmark mark='c'/> We can test a three-hundred-digit number for primality in milliseconds, which Part 30's cryptography depends on. <bookmark mark='d'/> And we can count a stream in a fraction of the memory. Each time, we pay with a small, provable chance of a wrong answer, or of a long wait.
625e7b6235f3.zh: 这就是这一部分的主题：抛一枚硬币可以代替聪明。<bookmark mark='a'/>有了硬币，我们可以在 n 的平方时间内检验一个声称的矩阵乘积，而不必重新计算。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们可以通过随机收缩边找到网络最薄弱的环节。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们可以在几毫秒内检验一个三百位的数是否为素数，第30部分的密码学就依赖于此。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们还可以用一小部分内存统计一个数据流。每一次，我们付出的代价是一个很小的、可以证明的概率：答案错误，或者等待很久。

aefb64f53010.en: Part 20 of Computer Science, Built: Randomness as a Resource. <bookmark mark='a'/> In this part: the two kinds of randomized algorithm, and how repetition shrinks their errors; checking products and polynomials with random points; cuts, primes, random walks and the power of two choices; Bloom filters and sketches of streams, ending in the Job in eighteen kilobytes; the probabilistic method; and whether the coins can be removed, and where they come from.
aefb64f53010.zh: 计算机科学，从零搭建，第20部分：作为资源的随机性。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一部分包括：两类随机算法，以及重复如何缩小它们的错误；用随机点检验乘积和多项式；割、素数、随机游走，以及两个选择的力量；布隆过滤器和数据流草图，最后是十八千字节里的作业；概率方法；以及硬币能否去掉、它们从哪里来。

dee3bb2f5e0c.en: Chapter one. Las Vegas and Monte Carlo.
dee3bb2f5e0c.zh: 第1章。拉斯维加斯与蒙特卡洛。

0db8f7780009.en: An algorithm that flips coins can gamble in two ways. <bookmark mark='a'/> A Las Vegas algorithm is always right, and only its running time depends on the coins. Randomized quicksort, from Part 16, is one. <bookmark mark='b'/> A Monte Carlo algorithm runs for a fixed time, and its answer may be wrong, with a probability we can bound and then make as small as we like. Most of this part is Monte Carlo. <bookmark mark='c'/> In both cases the randomness belongs to the algorithm. We assume nothing about the input: the guarantee holds for every input, averaged only over the algorithm's own coins.
0db8f7780009.zh: 一个抛硬币的算法可以用两种方式下注。<bookmark mark='a'/>拉斯维加斯算法总是正确，只有运行时间取决于硬币。第16部分的随机快速排序就是一例。<bookmark mark='b'/>蒙特卡洛算法运行固定的时间，它的答案可能出错，出错的概率我们可以给出上界，再让它要多小就有多小。这一部分的大多数算法是蒙特卡洛算法。<bookmark mark='c'/>两种情形中，随机性都属于算法本身。我们对输入不作任何假设：保证对每一个输入都成立，只对算法自己的硬币取平均。

57bba651505c.en: Here is a Las Vegas algorithm at work: quicksort with random pivots on 2,000 keys, run 400 times. Each bar counts the runs that made that many comparisons. <bookmark mark='a'/> The average was 24,761, and Part 16's exact formula predicts 24,730. <bookmark mark='b'/> The runs spread by about 1,339 either side, and the slowest made 30,234. <bookmark mark='c'/> The worst case, about two million comparisons, is possible in principle, but it needs a long run of terrible pivots, and its probability is far too small to observe. <bookmark mark='d'/> And every single run sorted the keys correctly. Only the time was a gamble.
57bba651505c.zh: 这是一个正在工作的拉斯维加斯算法：随机选主元的快速排序，作用于 2000 个键，运行 400 次。每根柱子统计做了那么多次比较的运行次数。<bookmark mark='a'/>平均值是 24761，第16部分的精确公式预测的是 24730。<bookmark mark='b'/>各次运行大约向两边分散 1339，最慢的一次做了 30234 次。<bookmark mark='c'/>最坏情形大约是两百万次比较，原则上可能发生，但它需要一长串糟糕的主元，概率小得根本观察不到。<bookmark mark='d'/>而每一次运行都正确地排好了序。只有时间是一场赌博。

3a40fcc20aa6.en: A Monte Carlo algorithm that errs half the time sounds useless. It isn't, because we can run it again. <bookmark mark='a'/> Many of this part's algorithms have one-sided error: when they say no, they are certainly right, and when they say yes, they are wrong with probability at most a half. Run one k times with fresh coins and believe yes only if every run says yes. All k must be fooled, and they are independent, so the error falls to a half to the k. <bookmark mark='b'/> Ten runs give one in a thousand. Forty give about one in a trillion, a smaller chance than that of the hardware itself failing during the computation. <bookmark mark='c'/> With error on both sides, say right with probability p above a half, take the majority of k runs. Hoeffding's inequality, from the AI series, says the majority is wrong with probability exponentially small in k.
3a40fcc20aa6.zh: 一个有一半时间出错的蒙特卡洛算法听起来毫无用处。其实不然，因为我们可以再运行一次。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一部分的许多算法只有单侧错误：它们说“否”时一定正确，说“是”时出错的概率至多为二分之一。用新的硬币运行 k 次，只有每次都说“是”才相信“是”。k 次必须全部被骗，而它们相互独立，所以错误降到二分之一的 k 次方。<bookmark mark='b'/>十次给出千分之一。四十次大约是万亿分之一，比硬件本身在计算过程中出故障的可能还小。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果两侧都会出错，比如以大于二分之一的概率 p 正确，就取 k 次运行的多数。人工智能系列中的霍夫丁不等式说，多数结果出错的概率随 k 指数地变小。

a718ae34b47c.en: Chapter two. Checking a product with a coin.

3a7843567326.en: Someone hands you two n by n matrices, A and B, and a third, C, and claims that C is their product. <bookmark mark='a'/> Checking by recomputing the product costs n cubed multiplications, or n to the 2.37 with the best methods of Part 19, which are impractical anyway. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 1977 Rūsiņš Freivalds suggested something cheaper. Flip n coins to make a random vector r of zeros and ones. Compute B times r, then A times that, and also C times r: three matrix-vector products, about three n squared operations. <bookmark mark='c'/> If the two vectors differ, C is certainly wrong. <bookmark mark='d'/> If they agree, C is probably right, and we can repeat with fresh coins. How probably?
3a7843567326.zh: 有人交给你两个 n 乘 n 的矩阵 A 和 B，以及第三个矩阵 C，声称 C 是它们的乘积。<bookmark mark='a'/>重新计算乘积来检验，要做 n 的三次方次乘法；用第19部分最好的方法是 n 的 2.37 次方，而那些方法反正也不实用。<bookmark mark='b'/>1977年，Rūsiņš Freivalds 提出了更便宜的办法。抛 n 枚硬币，得到一个由零和一组成的随机向量 r。先算 B 乘 r，再用 A 乘它，同时算 C 乘 r：三次矩阵与向量的乘法，大约三倍 n 的平方次运算。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果两个向量不同，C 肯定是错的。<bookmark mark='d'/>如果相同，C 大概是对的，我们可以用新的硬币再试。有多大概率是对的？

63f419b09cb6.en: Suppose C is wrong. <bookmark mark='a'/> Then the difference D, A B minus C, is not the zero matrix. <bookmark mark='b'/> Some entry, d i j, is nonzero, and the test passes only if D r is the zero vector, so in particular only if its i-th entry is zero. <bookmark mark='c'/> That entry is d i j times r j, plus a sum s over the other coins. <bookmark mark='d'/> Imagine flipping every coin except r j first. The coins are independent, so this changes nothing, but now s is a fixed number. <bookmark mark='e'/> For the entry to vanish, r j must equal minus s over d i j: one particular value. At most one of the two outcomes of r j can do that. <bookmark mark='f'/> So a wrong C passes with probability at most a half, whatever A, B and C are, and k independent rounds let it through with probability at most two to the minus k. <bookmark mark='g'/> The trick of revealing the coins in a convenient order is called the principle of deferred decisions, and we will use it again.
63f419b09cb6.zh: 假设 C 是错的。<bookmark mark='a'/>那么差 D，即 A B 减 C，不是零矩阵。<bookmark mark='b'/>它的某个元素 d i j 非零，而检验只有在 D r 是零向量时才通过，所以特别地，要求它的第 i 个分量为零。<bookmark mark='c'/>这个分量等于 d i j 乘 r j，再加上其他硬币贡献的和 s。<bookmark mark='d'/>想象先抛除 r j 以外的所有硬币。硬币是独立的，所以这不改变任何东西，但现在 s 是一个固定的数。<bookmark mark='e'/>要让这个分量为零，r j 必须等于负 s 除以 d i j：一个特定的值。r j 的两种结果中至多有一种能做到。<bookmark mark='f'/>所以无论 A、B、C 是什么，错误的 C 通过的概率至多为二分之一，k 轮独立检验让它通过的概率至多为二的负 k 次方。<bookmark mark='g'/>按方便的顺序揭开硬币的技巧叫作延迟决定原理，我们还会再用到它。

7b20ad858628.en: On this machine, with matrices of size 2000. <bookmark mark='a'/> Multiplying them takes sixteen billion floating-point operations, done by a heavily optimized library in about an eighth of a second. Checking takes twenty-four million operations. <bookmark mark='b'/> That is nearly seven hundred times fewer, but a matrix-vector product spends its time waiting for memory, so the check is only about 6 times faster in seconds, a reminder from Part 9. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now the error. We corrupted one entry of the product and tested it thousands of times. One round let it through about half the time, two rounds a quarter, and so on, right on the bound. <bookmark mark='d'/> With a single wrong entry the bound is tight, because only one coin matters. <bookmark mark='e'/> When many entries are wrong, many coins matter, and the wrong product never once got through.
7b20ad858628.zh: 在这台机器上，矩阵大小为 2000。<bookmark mark='a'/>把它们相乘需要一百六十亿次浮点运算，由一个高度优化的库完成，大约八分之一秒。检验需要两千四百万次运算。<bookmark mark='b'/>这少了将近七百倍，但矩阵与向量的乘法把时间花在等待内存上，所以按秒算，检验只快了大约 6 倍，这是第9部分的提醒。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在看错误。我们篡改了乘积的一个元素，检验了几千次。一轮检验大约一半的时间让它通过，两轮是四分之一，依此类推，正好落在上界上。<bookmark mark='d'/>只有一个元素错误时上界是紧的，因为只有一枚硬币起作用。<bookmark mark='e'/>当许多元素都错时，许多硬币起作用，错误的乘积一次也没有通过。

b660c95eeab7.en: Chapter three. Is this polynomial zero?
b660c95eeab7.zh: 第3章。这个多项式是零吗？

d5a3e560b875.en: Freivalds' check is a special case of a more general fact. <bookmark mark='a'/> A polynomial that is not identically zero can't vanish at too many points: if p has degree d and each variable is chosen at random from a set S, p is zero there with probability at most d over the size of S. This is the Schwartz–Zippel lemma, found independently by Schwartz, Zippel, and DeMillo with Lipton, around 1980. <bookmark mark='b'/> With one variable, it is the fact that a degree-d polynomial has at most d roots. <bookmark mark='c'/> With more, write p as a polynomial in the first variable with top power k. Either its top coefficient vanishes, with probability at most d minus k over S by induction, or p becomes a nonzero polynomial of degree k in one variable, which vanishes with probability at most k over S. The two add up to d over S.
d5a3e560b875.zh: Freivalds 的检验是一个更一般事实的特例。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个不恒为零的多项式不可能在太多点上为零：如果 p 的次数为 d，每个变量都从集合 S 中随机选取，那么 p 在该点为零的概率至多为 d 除以 S 的大小。这就是 Schwartz–Zippel 引理，大约在1980年由 Schwartz、Zippel，以及 DeMillo 与 Lipton 各自独立发现。<bookmark mark='b'/>只有一个变量时，它就是 d 次多项式至多有 d 个根这一事实。<bookmark mark='c'/>变量更多时，把 p 写成第一个变量的多项式，最高次数为 k。要么它的最高次系数为零，由归纳假设，概率至多为 d 减 k 除以 S；要么 p 成为一个变量的非零 k 次多项式，为零的概率至多为 k 除以 S。两者相加是 d 除以 S。

c55d2c9327ab.en: Here is a claimed identity: the product x minus y, times y minus z, times z minus x, against an expansion. <bookmark mark='a'/> Instead of expanding, substitute random numbers and compare. We did this twenty thousand times for each size of S. <bookmark mark='b'/> The claim is false: one sign is wrong, so the two sides differ by two x z squared, a polynomial of degree three. It vanishes only when x or z is zero, which is why the agreement rates sit a little under the lemma's bound of three over S. With a thousand values, one test in five hundred is fooled; twenty tests are fooled with probability below ten to the minus fifty. <bookmark mark='c'/> The idea scales. The determinant of an eight by eight Vandermonde matrix equals a product of differences, a polynomial with forty thousand terms if you expand it. Evaluating both sides at fifty random points modulo a large prime took a fraction of a millisecond each, and they agreed every time.
c55d2c9327ab.zh: 这是一个声称的恒等式：x 减 y，乘 y 减 z，再乘 z 减 x，与一个展开式。<bookmark mark='a'/>不去展开，而是代入随机数并比较。对 S 的每个大小，我们做了两万次。<bookmark mark='b'/>这个声称是错的：有一个符号写错了，所以两边相差二倍 x z 的平方，一个三次多项式。它只在 x 或 z 为零时为零，这就是为什么一致率比引理的界三除以 S 稍低一点。S 有一千个值时，五百次检验中被骗一次；二十次检验全被骗的概率低于十的负五十次方。<bookmark mark='c'/>这个想法可以推广。八乘八范德蒙德矩阵的行列式等于一个差的乘积，展开后是一个有四万项的多项式。在五十个随机点上对一个大素数取模来计算两边，每次只要不到一毫秒，而且每次都一致。

c8fd963da6e6.en: A less obvious polynomial. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take a graph, and build its Tutte matrix: for each edge i j, put a variable x i j above the diagonal and minus x i j below it. <bookmark mark='b'/> For this graph the determinant is a perfect square, and each of its two terms is a perfect matching, a set of edges that covers every vertex exactly once. <bookmark mark='c'/> William Tutte proved in 1947 that the determinant is a nonzero polynomial exactly when the graph has a perfect matching. But it can have exponentially many terms. <bookmark mark='d'/> László Lovász saw in 1979 that we never need to expand it: substitute random numbers modulo a prime and compute one determinant by elimination, Schwartz–Zippel bounding the error. <bookmark mark='e'/> We tried it on forty-eight random graphs near the threshold where matchings appear. 33 had one, and the determinant agreed with Edmonds' blossom algorithm every time. Determinants parallelize well, so this became the route to fast parallel matching algorithms.
c8fd963da6e6.zh: 一个不那么明显的多项式。<bookmark mark='a'/>取一个图，构造它的 Tutte 矩阵：对每条边 i j，在对角线上方放一个变量 x i j，下方放负 x i j。<bookmark mark='b'/>对这个图，行列式是一个完全平方，它的两项各对应一个完美匹配，即恰好覆盖每个顶点一次的一组边。<bookmark mark='c'/>William Tutte 在1947年证明，图有完美匹配当且仅当这个行列式是非零多项式。但它可能有指数多项。<bookmark mark='d'/>László Lovász 在1979年看出我们根本不必展开它：代入模一个素数的随机数，用消元法算一次行列式，错误由 Schwartz–Zippel 控制。<bookmark mark='e'/>我们在四十八个随机图上试了它，这些图都在匹配开始出现的阈值附近。其中 33 个有完美匹配，行列式每次都与 Edmonds 的开花算法一致。行列式很适合并行计算，所以这成了快速并行匹配算法的途径。

27b1f9d4cba9.en: One more use of the same idea. <bookmark mark='a'/> Alice has the novels, twenty-five megabytes, and Bob has a copy that may differ. Sending the whole file to compare is expensive. <bookmark mark='b'/> Instead, Alice treats her file as one enormous number a, picks a random sixty-one-bit prime p, and sends p and a modulo p: sixteen bytes. Bob compares with his own number modulo p. <bookmark mark='c'/> We flipped a single bit of Bob's copy. The two remainders differ completely, and computing one took about a seventh of a second. <bookmark mark='d'/> When could different files give the same remainder? Only if p divides their difference, a number with two hundred million bits. Such a number has at most a few million prime factors as large as p, out of tens of quadrillions of primes that size. So the chance of a false match is about one in ten billion, and a second prime squares it. Part 21 turns this into Rabin and Karp's string search, rolling the remainder along the text.
27b1f9d4cba9.zh: 同一个想法的另一个用途。<bookmark mark='a'/>Alice 有这些小说，两千五百万字节，Bob 有一份可能不同的副本。为了比较而传送整个文件代价太高。<bookmark mark='b'/>Alice 把她的文件看成一个巨大的数 a，随机选一个六十一位的素数 p，发送 p 和 a 模 p：十六个字节。Bob 用他自己的数模 p 来比较。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们把 Bob 副本中的一个比特翻转了。两个余数完全不同，计算一个大约要七分之一秒。<bookmark mark='d'/>不同的文件什么时候会给出相同的余数？只有当 p 整除它们的差时，而这个差是一个有两亿个比特的数。这样的数至多有几百万个与 p 一样大的素因子，而这么大的素数有几亿亿个。所以误判的概率大约是百亿分之一，换第二个素数再试一次，就把它平方。第21部分把这变成 Rabin 与 Karp 的字符串搜索，让余数沿着文本滚动。

9eb1f4d8386a.en: Chapter four. A minimum cut by contraction.

07b7e1131950.en: A cut of a graph splits its vertices into two sides; its size is the number of edges between them. This graph has two dense clusters joined by three edges, so its minimum cut has size three. Finding a minimum cut is a classic problem, usually solved with maximum flows. <bookmark mark='a'/> David Karger's algorithm, from 1993, is almost embarrassingly simple. Pick an edge at random and contract it: merge its two ends into one vertex, keep all the other edges, and throw away the loops. Repeat until two vertices are left. The edges between them are a cut. <bookmark mark='b'/> This run kept all three bridges to the end and found the minimum cut.
07b7e1131950.zh: 图的一个割把顶点分成两边；割的大小是两边之间的边数。这个图有两个稠密的簇，由三条边相连，所以它的最小割大小为三。求最小割是一个经典问题，通常用最大流来解。<bookmark mark='a'/>David Karger 1993年的算法简单得几乎令人难为情。随机选一条边并收缩它：把它的两个端点合并成一个顶点，保留所有其他边，丢掉自环。重复直到只剩两个顶点。它们之间的边就是一个割。<bookmark mark='b'/>这一次运行把三座桥一直保留到最后，找到了最小割。

cec29bca133e.en: Run it again with other coins. <bookmark mark='a'/> This time a bridge was contracted along the way, and the two clusters were merged. <bookmark mark='b'/> What is left cuts a single vertex off from the rest, a cut of size 5. Each run can fail, so how often does it succeed?
cec29bca133e.zh: 用别的硬币再运行一次。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一次，途中有一座桥被收缩了，两个簇被合并在一起。<bookmark mark='b'/>剩下的结果是把单个顶点与其余部分切开，一个大小为 5 的割。每次运行都可能失败，那么它多常成功？

1eca6895706a.en: The analysis is as short as the algorithm. Fix a minimum cut C, of size k. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every vertex has at least k edges, because otherwise the edges around that one vertex would be a smaller cut. <bookmark mark='b'/> So there are at least n k over two edges, and the first random edge lands in C with probability at most two over n. <bookmark mark='c'/> Contracting never creates a smaller cut, so the same argument works at every step, with n minus one vertices, then n minus two, and so on. <bookmark mark='d'/> C survives to the end if it survives every step. Write the product out, and almost everything cancels: <bookmark mark='e'/> the success probability is at least two over n times n minus one, one over n choose two. <bookmark mark='f'/> There is a free corollary. A specific minimum cut is the output with at least that probability, and different cuts are different outcomes, so no graph has more than n choose two minimum cuts.
1eca6895706a.zh: 分析和算法一样短。固定一个大小为 k 的最小割 C。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个顶点至少有 k 条边，否则这一个顶点周围的边就构成一个更小的割。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以至少有 n k 除以二条边，第一条随机边落在 C 中的概率至多为二除以 n。<bookmark mark='c'/>收缩从不产生更小的割，所以同样的论证在每一步都成立，先是 n 减一个顶点，再是 n 减二个，依此类推。<bookmark mark='d'/>C 能存活到最后，当且仅当它在每一步都存活。把乘积写出来，几乎所有项都消掉了：<bookmark mark='e'/>成功概率至少是二除以 n 乘 n 减一，即 n 选二分之一。<bookmark mark='f'/>还有一个免费的推论。一个特定的最小割至少以这个概率成为输出，而不同的割是不同的结果，所以没有哪个图的最小割超过 n 选二个。

429a6dda459f.en: We ran the contraction twenty thousand times on the two-cluster graph. Each bar counts the runs that ended with a cut of that size. <bookmark mark='a'/> The minimum cut came out in 13% of runs. The bound promised at least one in a hundred and twenty, under one percent, so on this graph the truth is about fifteen times better. <bookmark mark='b'/> The bound is a worst case, and repetition does the rest: run it n choose two times log n times and keep the smallest cut, and it is wrong with probability at most one over n. <bookmark mark='c'/> The worst case is real. In a ring of ten vertices, any two of the ten edges form a minimum cut, which makes forty-five of them, exactly n choose two. The runs found all forty-five, each about once in forty-five tries, so here the bound is exact.
429a6dda459f.zh: 我们在双簇图上运行了两万次收缩。每根柱子统计结果为该大小的割的运行次数。<bookmark mark='a'/>最小割出现在 13% 的运行中。上界保证至少一百二十分之一，不到百分之一，所以在这个图上实际情况大约好十五倍。<bookmark mark='b'/>上界是最坏情形，其余的交给重复：运行 n 选二乘 log n 次，保留最小的割，出错的概率至多为 n 分之一。<bookmark mark='c'/>最坏情形是真实存在的。在一个十个顶点的环中，十条边中任意两条都构成一个最小割，一共四十五个，正好是 n 选二。各次运行找到了全部四十五个，每个大约四十五次中出现一次，所以这里上界是精确的。

092bca0c6570.en: Where is the waste? <bookmark mark='a'/> Early contractions almost never hit the minimum cut, <bookmark mark='b'/> so all the risk is at the end. <bookmark mark='c'/> Karger and Clifford Stein, in 1996, contract only to about n over root two vertices, where the cut survives with probability at least a half, <bookmark mark='d'/> then recurse twice and keep the better result. <bookmark mark='e'/> That takes n squared log n time, and succeeds with probability about one over log n instead of one over n squared. <bookmark mark='f'/> On our forty-eight-vertex test graph, a single plain contraction succeeded 18% of the time; Karger–Stein succeeded in all forty of its runs.
092bca0c6570.zh: 浪费在哪里？<bookmark mark='a'/>早期的收缩几乎从不碰到最小割，<bookmark mark='b'/>所以所有风险都在最后。<bookmark mark='c'/>Karger 与 Clifford Stein 在1996年只收缩到大约 n 除以根号二个顶点，这时割仍以至少二分之一的概率存活，<bookmark mark='d'/>然后递归两次，保留较好的结果。<bookmark mark='e'/>这需要 n 平方 log n 的时间，成功概率大约是一除以 log n，而不是一除以 n 的平方。<bookmark mark='f'/>在我们四十八个顶点的测试图上，一次普通收缩成功的比例是 18%；Karger–Stein 的四十次运行全部成功。

bd762d952345.en: Part 30 will need prime numbers three hundred digits long, and lots of them. Testing one by trial division would take ten to the hundred and fifty divisions. <bookmark mark='a'/> Fermat's little theorem gives a shortcut. If n is prime, then for every a not divisible by n, a to the n minus one is one, modulo n. <bookmark mark='b'/> So if we find an a where it isn't, n is certainly composite. Two to the ninetieth, modulo ninety-one, is sixty-four, <bookmark mark='c'/> so ninety-one is composite, and we learned that without finding a factor. <bookmark mark='d'/> But some bases lie. Three to the ninetieth is one modulo ninety-one, as if ninety-one were prime. <bookmark mark='e'/> Each test is cheap: repeated squaring computes the power with about one squaring per bit of n.
bd762d952345.zh: 第30部分需要三百位长的素数，而且需要很多。用试除法检验一个，要做十的一百五十次方次除法。<bookmark mark='a'/>费马小定理给出了一条捷径。如果 n 是素数，那么对每个不被 n 整除的 a，a 的 n 减一次方模 n 等于一。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以只要找到一个 a 使它不等于一，n 就一定是合数。二的九十次方模九十一是六十四，<bookmark mark='c'/>所以九十一是合数，而我们没有找到任何因子就知道了这一点。<bookmark mark='d'/>但有些底数会说谎。三的九十次方模九十一是一，就好像九十一是素数一样。<bookmark mark='e'/>每次检验都很便宜：反复平方法计算这个幂，n 的每一位大约只需一次平方。

a8f3362c2dcb.en: Worse, some composites fool every base. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are the bases from one to five hundred and sixty for n equals five hundred and sixty-one, which is three times eleven times seventeen. Every base that shares no factor with it, all 320 of them, passes Fermat's test. <bookmark mark='b'/> Alwin Korselt explained why in 1899: this happens exactly when n is squarefree and p minus one divides n minus one for each of its prime factors p. Five hundred and sixty is divisible by two, ten and sixteen. <bookmark mark='c'/> Robert Carmichael found the first examples in 1910. There are 43 below a million, and in 1994 Alford, Granville and Pomerance proved there are infinitely many. Fermat's test needs repairing.
a8f3362c2dcb.zh: 更糟的是，有些合数能骗过所有底数。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里是 n 等于五百六十一时从一到五百六十的底数，五百六十一等于三乘十一乘十七。每个与它没有公因子的底数，全部 320 个，都通过了费马检验。<bookmark mark='b'/>Alwin Korselt 在1899年解释了原因：这种情况恰好在 n 无平方因子、且对它的每个素因子 p，p 减一都整除 n 减一时发生。五百六十能被二、十和十六整除。<bookmark mark='c'/>Robert Carmichael 在1910年找到了最早的例子。一百万以下有 43 个，1994年 Alford、Granville 与 Pomerance 证明了它们有无穷多个。费马检验需要修补。

cac42d56af41.en: Gary Miller in 1976 and Michael Rabin in 1980 found the repair. <bookmark mark='a'/> Modulo a prime, the only square roots of one are one and minus one, because x squared minus one factors as x minus one times x plus one, and in a field a product is zero only if a factor is. <bookmark mark='b'/> Write n minus one as a power of two times an odd number d, and compute a to the d, then keep squaring until we reach a to the n minus one. <bookmark mark='c'/> For a prime, the sequence is all ones, or it hits minus one somewhere before the first one. <bookmark mark='d'/> Watch five hundred and sixty-one with base two: two hundred and sixty-three, one hundred and sixty-six, sixty-seven, then one. <bookmark mark='e'/> Sixty-seven squares to one but isn't plus or minus one: a square root of one that no prime can have. Fermat was fooled; this test isn't. <bookmark mark='f'/> Rabin proved that for every odd composite, at most a quarter of the bases lie. Five hundred and sixty-one has only 10. <bookmark mark='g'/> Searching every odd composite below twenty thousand, the worst was nine, with exactly a quarter, so the bound can't be improved. Forty random bases give an error below four to the minus forty, about ten to the minus twenty-four.
cac42d56af41.zh: Gary Miller 在1976年、Michael Rabin 在1980年找到了修补的办法。<bookmark mark='a'/>模一个素数，一的平方根只有一和负一，因为 x 的平方减一分解为 x 减一乘 x 加一，而在域中，乘积为零仅当某个因子为零。<bookmark mark='b'/>把 n 减一写成二的幂乘一个奇数 d，先算 a 的 d 次方，再不断平方，直到 a 的 n 减一次方。<bookmark mark='c'/>对素数来说，这个序列要么全是一，要么在第一个一之前的某处出现负一。<bookmark mark='d'/>看五百六十一取底数二：二百六十三、一百六十六、六十七，然后是一。<bookmark mark='e'/>六十七的平方是一，但它既不是一也不是负一：这是任何素数都不可能有的一的平方根。费马检验被骗了，这个检验没有。<bookmark mark='f'/>Rabin 证明，对每个奇合数，至多四分之一的底数会说谎。五百六十一只有 10 个。<bookmark mark='g'/>搜索两万以下的每个奇合数，最坏的是九，恰好四分之一，所以这个界不能改进。四十个随机底数给出的错误低于四的负四十次方，大约十的负二十四次方。

fc172134a202.en: Now we can find big primes: pick random odd numbers of the right size, and keep the first that passes forty rounds. <bookmark mark='a'/> About one number in log n near n is prime, so a 1024-bit search tries about three hundred and fifty odd candidates. <bookmark mark='b'/> Almost all fail the first round, three milliseconds here, and a 1024-bit prime took about a second in plain Python. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2002, Manindra Agrawal, Neeraj Kayal and Nitin Saxena found a deterministic polynomial-time test, settling a very old question. But it is far slower, <bookmark mark='d'/> and every cryptographic library still flips coins.
fc172134a202.zh: 现在我们可以找大素数了：随机选大小合适的奇数，保留第一个通过四十轮检验的。<bookmark mark='a'/>n 附近大约每 log n 个数中有一个素数，所以一次 1024 位的搜索大约要试三百五十个奇数候选。<bookmark mark='b'/>几乎所有候选在第一轮就失败，在这里一轮要三毫秒，用纯 Python 找一个 1024 位素数大约用了一秒。<bookmark mark='c'/>2002年，Manindra Agrawal、Neeraj Kayal 与 Nitin Saxena 找到了一个多项式时间的确定性检验，解决了一个非常古老的问题。但它慢得多，<bookmark mark='d'/>每个密码学库仍然在抛硬币。

b351da465561.en: Chapter six. Random walks that solve SAT.
b351da465561.zh: 第6章。求解 SAT 的随机游走。

609df8b1e2e0.en: A 2-SAT formula is an and of clauses, each an or of two literals. Part 18 solved it exactly, with strongly connected components of the implication graph. <bookmark mark='a'/> Christos Papadimitriou analyzed a much dumber method in 1991. Start anywhere. While some clause fails, pick one, and flip one of its two variables, chosen by a coin. <bookmark mark='b'/> It uses no structure at all. Why should it ever finish?
609df8b1e2e0.zh: 2-SAT 公式是若干子句的合取，每个子句是两个文字的析取。第18部分用蕴含图的强连通分量精确地解决了它。<bookmark mark='a'/>Christos Papadimitriou 在1991年分析了一种笨得多的方法。从任意赋值开始。只要有子句不成立，就挑一个，用硬币选它的两个变量之一并翻转。<bookmark mark='b'/>它完全不利用结构。凭什么它会结束？

f3703dd794ab.en: Fix one satisfying assignment, x star, and let D be the number of variables where our assignment differs from it. <bookmark mark='a'/> A clause that fails has both its literals false, but x star makes at least one of them true, so we disagree with x star on at least one of the two variables. <bookmark mark='b'/> Flipping a random one of the two moves D one step closer to zero with probability at least a half. <bookmark mark='c'/> So D does a random walk on the line from zero to n, pushed toward zero at least as often as away. This is the gambler's ruin. From any start, the expected time to reach zero is at most n squared. <bookmark mark='d'/> Here is one walk, starting eight steps away. It took 178 flips. We may even stop sooner, at some other solution. <bookmark mark='e'/> So run two n squared steps. If the formula is satisfiable, Markov's inequality says we fail with probability at most a half, and repetition does the rest. The bound is for the worst formula: on random satisfiable ones, with up to three hundred and twenty variables, the walk needed only about two flips per variable.
f3703dd794ab.zh: 固定一个满足赋值 x 星，令 D 为我们的赋值与它不同的变量个数。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个不成立的子句两个文字都为假，但 x 星至少使其中一个为真，所以在这两个变量中，我们至少有一个与 x 星不同。<bookmark mark='b'/>随机翻转两者之一，以至少二分之一的概率使 D 向零靠近一步。<bookmark mark='c'/>于是 D 在从零到 n 的直线上做随机游走，被推向零的次数至少和远离的一样多。这就是赌徒破产问题。从任何起点出发，到达零的期望时间至多为 n 的平方。<bookmark mark='d'/>这是一次游走，从八步之外开始。它用了 178 次翻转。我们甚至可能更早停下，停在另一个解上。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以运行二倍 n 平方步。如果公式可满足，马尔可夫不等式说我们失败的概率至多为二分之一，其余的交给重复。这个上界针对最坏的公式：在多达三百二十个变量的随机可满足公式上，游走每个变量只需要大约两次翻转。

d465b0a69da4.en: For 3-SAT the same walk works, but worse. <bookmark mark='a'/> A failing clause now has three variables, and only one of them might be the right one to flip, so D falls with probability only a third. <bookmark mark='b'/> The walk drifts away from the solution, so Uwe Schöning, in 1999, restarts it from a fresh random assignment every three n flips. <bookmark mark='c'/> A careful count shows each restart succeeds with probability about three quarters to the n, so about four thirds to the n restarts are enough: exponential, but far fewer than the two to the n assignments. <bookmark mark='d'/> We tested it on the hardest small instances we could make, random formulas at the threshold with exactly one satisfying assignment, checked by brute force. <bookmark mark='e'/> With 20 variables, the walk needed about 33 restarts on average, under Schöning's bound, which is for the worst case, where brute force has about a million assignments to try. The best algorithms known today, descendants of Paturi, Pudlák, Saks and Zane's, get down to about one point three to the n. Whether something much better exists is the question behind the exponential time hypothesis of Part 27.
d465b0a69da4.zh: 对 3-SAT，同样的游走也行，但更差。<bookmark mark='a'/>现在一个不成立的子句有三个变量，其中可能只有一个是该翻转的，所以 D 下降的概率只有三分之一。<bookmark mark='b'/>游走会远离解，所以 Uwe Schöning 在1999年每翻转三倍 n 次就从一个新的随机赋值重新开始。<bookmark mark='c'/>仔细计算表明，每次重启成功的概率大约是四分之三的 n 次方，所以大约四分之三的倒数的 n 次方次重启就够了：仍是指数，但远少于二的 n 次方个赋值。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们在能造出的最难的小实例上测试了它：阈值处恰有一个满足赋值的随机公式，用穷举法核实。<bookmark mark='e'/>有 20 个变量时，游走平均需要大约 33 次重启，低于针对最坏情形的 Schöning 上界，而穷举法要试大约一百万个赋值。今天已知最好的算法，Paturi、Pudlák、Saks 与 Zane 算法的后继者，能降到大约一点三的 n 次方。是否存在好得多的算法，正是第27部分指数时间假设背后的问题。

0096591fcb11.en: Chapter seven. Balls into bins, and the power of two choices.
0096591fcb11.zh: 第7章。球与箱，以及两个选择的力量。

95cc23a8472c.en: Throw balls into bins at random. How full does the fullest bin get? This question decides how well a hash table's chains, Part 17, or a server farm's queues are balanced. <bookmark mark='a'/> On the left, each of twenty-four balls goes into one random bin of twelve. On the right, each ball looks at two random bins and goes into the emptier one. <bookmark mark='b'/> The same random numbers drive both sides: the left uses the first choice, the right uses both. <bookmark mark='c'/> One choice leaves some bins empty and piles others high. Two choices are strikingly even.
95cc23a8472c.zh: 把球随机扔进箱子。最满的箱子会有多满？这个问题决定了哈希表的链（第17部分）或服务器集群的队列平衡得有多好。<bookmark mark='a'/>左边，二十四个球各自进入十二个箱子中的一个随机箱子。右边，每个球看两个随机箱子，进入较空的那个。<bookmark mark='b'/>两边由同样的随机数驱动：左边用第一个选择，右边两个都用。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个选择会让一些箱子空着，另一些堆得很高。两个选择则出奇地均匀。

34ddc0c169bd.en: Now with n balls and n bins, for n from a thousand to a million. <bookmark mark='a'/> With one choice the fullest bin holds about log n over log log n balls; the column beside it is that formula, which is right only up to a factor that tends to one very slowly, so the measured loads are higher. <bookmark mark='b'/> With two choices the fullest bin holds about log log n over log two, plus a constant. For a million balls: ten against four. <bookmark mark='c'/> At a million, the one-choice loads follow a Poisson law, a fraction e to the minus one over k factorial of the bins holding k, with 9 unlucky bins holding 8. With two choices nothing went above 4. A tiny change in the rule, an exponential change in the result. This is the power of two choices, from Azar, Broder, Karlin and Upfal in 1994.
34ddc0c169bd.zh: 现在是 n 个球和 n 个箱子，n 从一千到一百万。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个选择时，最满的箱子大约有 log n 除以 log log n 个球；旁边一列就是这个公式，它只在一个非常缓慢地趋于一的因子之内正确，所以测得的负载更高。<bookmark mark='b'/>两个选择时，最满的箱子大约有 log log n 除以 log 二个球，再加一个常数。一百万个球时：十对四。<bookmark mark='c'/>在一百万时，一个选择的负载服从泊松分布，装有 k 个球的箱子占 e 的负一次方除以 k 的阶乘，有 9 个倒霉的箱子装了 8 个。两个选择时没有超过 4 的。规则上一个微小的改变，结果上一个指数级的改变。这就是两个选择的力量，来自 Azar、Broder、Karlin 与 Upfal 1994年的工作。

7f9f1e4f57ad.en: Why? <bookmark mark='a'/> Let beta i be the number of bins holding at least i balls. <bookmark mark='b'/> A ball lands at height i plus one only if both its bins already hold at least i, <bookmark mark='c'/> with probability about beta i over n, squared. So each height's fraction is about the square of the one below. <bookmark mark='d'/> Squaring collapses fast: a quarter, a sixteenth, one in two hundred and fifty-six, one in sixty-five thousand, below one over n after about log log n steps. <bookmark mark='e'/> With one choice there is no squaring, only one over k factorial. <bookmark mark='f'/> With d choices the load is log log n over log d, so most of the gain is in the second choice. <bookmark mark='g'/> Load balancers use exactly this rule, and cuckoo hashing gives every key two homes.
7f9f1e4f57ad.zh: 为什么？<bookmark mark='a'/>令 beta i 为至少装有 i 个球的箱子数。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个球只有在它的两个箱子都已至少有 i 个球时，才会落在第 i 加一层，<bookmark mark='c'/>概率大约是 beta i 除以 n 的平方。所以每一层的比例大约是下一层比例的平方。<bookmark mark='d'/>平方让它迅速崩塌：四分之一、十六分之一、二百五十六分之一、六万五千分之一，大约 log log n 步之后就低于 n 分之一。<bookmark mark='e'/>一个选择时没有平方，只有 k 的阶乘分之一。<bookmark mark='f'/>d 个选择时负载是 log log n 除以 log d，所以大部分收益来自第二个选择。<bookmark mark='g'/>负载均衡器正是用这条规则，布谷鸟哈希给每个键两个位置。

9d5d5c3f7a85.en: In 1970 Burton Bloom asked how to test membership in a set using far less memory than the set itself, if we accept an occasional wrong yes. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take an array of bits, all zero, and three hash functions. <bookmark mark='b'/> To add a word, hash it three times and set those three bits. Here go six words from Moby-Dick. <bookmark mark='c'/> The words themselves are not stored anywhere. Only bits remain.
9d5d5c3f7a85.zh: 1970年，Burton Bloom 问：如果偶尔接受一个错误的“是”，能否用远少于集合本身的内存来检验成员关系？<bookmark mark='a'/>取一个全为零的比特数组和三个哈希函数。<bookmark mark='b'/>要加入一个词，就把它哈希三次，把那三个比特置一。这里加入《白鲸》中的六个词。<bookmark mark='c'/>词本身没有存在任何地方。只剩下比特。

f3d99ca85687.en: To ask whether a word is in the set, check its three bits. <bookmark mark='a'/> Dog: one of its bits is zero, so dog was certainly never added. <bookmark mark='b'/> Boat: also a zero, certainly not. <bookmark mark='c'/> Ocean: all three of its bits are set, by whale, so the filter says yes, wrongly. A false positive. <bookmark mark='d'/> Deck: also yes, its bits set by harpoon and Queequeg. A Bloom filter never says no to a word that is in the set, but it sometimes says yes to one that isn't. How often?
f3d99ca85687.zh: 要问一个词是否在集合中，就检查它的三个比特。<bookmark mark='a'/>dog：它有一个比特是零，所以 dog 肯定从未加入。<bookmark mark='b'/>boat：也有一个零，肯定不在。<bookmark mark='c'/>ocean：它的三个比特都被 whale 置了一，所以过滤器说“是”，错了。这是一个假阳性。<bookmark mark='d'/>deck：也说“是”，它的比特由 harpoon 和 Queequeg 置一。布隆过滤器对集合中的词从不说“否”，但有时对不在集合中的词说“是”。这有多常见？

f7015857ccc9.en: Suppose we add n words to m bits with k hash functions, and pretend the hashes are truly random. <bookmark mark='a'/> A particular bit is missed by all k n hashes with probability one minus one over m, to the k n, which is about e to the minus k n over m. <bookmark mark='b'/> A word that was never added is a false positive if all k of its bits happen to be set: probability about one minus that, to the k. <bookmark mark='c'/> There is a balance. With few hash functions each probe is likely to hit a set bit; with many, the array fills up. <bookmark mark='d'/> Calculus gives the best k, m over n times log two, and at that point exactly half the bits are set. The error is then about 0.6185 to the power m over n. <bookmark mark='e'/> Every extra bit per word divides the error by about 1.6, and ten bits per word give about one percent, whatever the words are and however long.
f7015857ccc9.zh: 假设我们用 k 个哈希函数把 n 个词加入 m 个比特，并假定哈希真正随机。<bookmark mark='a'/>某个特定比特被全部 k n 次哈希错过的概率是一减 m 分之一的 k n 次方，约等于 e 的负 k n 除以 m 次方。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个从未加入的词，如果它的 k 个比特恰好都被置一，就是假阳性：概率约为一减去上面那个数，再取 k 次方。<bookmark mark='c'/>这里有一个平衡。哈希函数少，每次探查很可能碰到置一的比特；哈希函数多，数组会被填满。<bookmark mark='d'/>微积分给出最好的 k，即 m 除以 n 乘 log 二，此时恰好一半的比特被置一。错误率约为 0.6185 的 m 除以 n 次方。<bookmark mark='e'/>每个词每多一个比特，错误率大约除以 1.6，每个词十个比特给出大约百分之一，无论词是什么、有多长。

3131e4789b95.en: Now a real one: all 57,895 distinct words of the novels, ten bits per word, queried with a hundred thousand random strings that are not words of the novels. <bookmark mark='a'/> The purple curve is the formula, and the green dots are what we measured for each number of hash functions. <bookmark mark='b'/> At the best k, seven, 0.81 percent of the non-words slipped through, against a predicted 0.82, and almost exactly half the bits were set. <bookmark mark='c'/> With sixteen bits per word the rate falls to one in two thousand. <bookmark mark='d'/> The filter takes seventy kilobytes, while just the letters of the words take four hundred and forty, and it never missed a word that was there. <bookmark mark='e'/> Counting filters allow deletions, cuckoo filters do better at low error rates, and nearly every log-structured database keeps a Bloom filter per file to skip disk reads, as Part 34 will show.
3131e4789b95.zh: 现在看一个真实的：小说中全部 57895 个不同的词，每个词十个比特，用十万个不是小说中词的随机字符串来查询。<bookmark mark='a'/>紫色曲线是公式，绿色的点是我们对每个哈希函数个数测得的值。<bookmark mark='b'/>在最好的 k 即七时，有百分之 0.81 的非词溜了过去，预测值是 0.82，而且几乎恰好一半的比特被置一。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个词十六个比特时，这个比例降到两千分之一。<bookmark mark='d'/>过滤器占七十千字节，而光是这些词的字母就要四百四十千字节，它也从没漏掉一个真正在集合中的词。<bookmark mark='e'/>计数过滤器允许删除，布谷鸟过滤器在低错误率时更好，几乎每个日志结构的数据库都为每个文件保存一个布隆过滤器来跳过磁盘读取，第34部分会展示这一点。

201e4232e6ac.en: Chapter nine. Streams: one pass, little memory.
201e4232e6ac.zh: 第9章。数据流：一遍扫描，很少的内存。

8f3c608ef031.en: Part 17 kept every distinct word of the novels, almost fifty-eight thousand. What if we can't afford that? <bookmark mark='a'/> In the streaming model the items go by once, <bookmark mark='b'/> can't be stored, <bookmark mark='c'/> and memory is far smaller than the stream, often smaller than the number of different items in it. <bookmark mark='d'/> Routers, sensors, logs and query planners live in this world.
8f3c608ef031.zh: 第17部分保存了小说中的每个不同的词，将近五万八千个。如果我们负担不起呢？<bookmark mark='a'/>在流模型中，数据项只经过一次，<bookmark mark='b'/>无法存下来，<bookmark mark='c'/>而内存远小于数据流，往往比其中不同数据项的个数还小。<bookmark mark='d'/>路由器、传感器、日志和查询规划器都生活在这个世界里。

5275061aeb45.en: First, a fair sample. We want k items chosen uniformly from the stream, but we don't know how long it will be. <bookmark mark='a'/> Reservoir sampling, as Jeffrey Vitter described it in 1985: keep the first k. When the i-th item arrives, keep it with probability k over i, throwing out a random one of the k. <bookmark mark='b'/> By induction, every item seen so far is in the sample with probability exactly k over i. An item stays when the next one arrives unless the newcomer is kept and picks its slot, and the arithmetic turns k over i into k over i plus one. <bookmark mark='c'/> We drew five items from a hundred, fifty thousand times: every item was picked close to the expected two thousand five hundred times. <bookmark mark='d'/> And here are eight words drawn uniformly from all four million six hundred thousand in the novels, in a single pass.
5275061aeb45.zh: 首先，一个公平的样本。我们想从数据流中均匀地选出 k 项，但不知道它会有多长。<bookmark mark='a'/>蓄水池抽样，按 Jeffrey Vitter 1985年的描述：保留前 k 项。第 i 项到来时，以 k 除以 i 的概率保留它，并随机扔掉 k 项中的一项。<bookmark mark='b'/>由归纳法，到目前为止见过的每一项都恰好以 k 除以 i 的概率在样本中。当下一项到来时，一项留下，除非新来者被保留并选中了它的位置，算一下，k 除以 i 就变成 k 除以 i 加一。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们从一百项中抽五项，抽了五万次：每一项被选中的次数都接近期望的两千五百次。<bookmark mark='d'/>这里是从小说全部四百六十万个词中一遍扫描、均匀抽出的八个词。

482e37bdba4e.en: Next, the frequent items, the Job's own question. <bookmark mark='a'/> Jayadev Misra and David Gries gave a deterministic method in 1982, with k minus one counters. A word that has a counter adds one. A new word takes a free counter. A new word with no free counter subtracts one from every counter, and the counters that reach zero are freed. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each subtraction cancels k words at once, the new one and one from each counter, so it can happen at most n over k times. So every count is low by at most n over k, and any word more frequent than n over k must survive. <bookmark mark='c'/> With ninety-nine counters on the novels, n over k is about forty-six thousand. The thirteen words above that all survived, each undercounted by about thirty-nine thousand, and words below it may vanish. A second pass, counting only the survivors, makes the counts exact. But the estimates themselves are poor. Can coin flips do better?
482e37bdba4e.zh: 接下来是频繁项，正是作业自己的问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>Jayadev Misra 与 David Gries 在1982年给出了一个确定性方法，用 k 减一个计数器。已有计数器的词加一。新词占用一个空闲计数器。没有空闲计数器的新词让每个计数器减一，减到零的计数器被释放。<bookmark mark='b'/>每次减法一次抵消 k 个词：新来的一个，以及每个计数器各一个，所以它至多发生 n 除以 k 次。因此每个计数至多偏低 n 除以 k，任何比 n 除以 k 更频繁的词一定留存下来。<bookmark mark='c'/>在小说上用九十九个计数器，n 除以 k 大约是四万六千。高于它的十三个词全部留存，每个大约少计三万九千，低于它的词可能消失。第二遍扫描，只统计留存下来的词，就能得到精确的计数。但估计值本身很差。硬币能做得更好吗？

bcc4efd81d7b.en: Graham Cormode and S. Muthukrishnan's Count-Min sketch, from 2005, keeps a small table: d rows of w counters, with an independent hash function for each row. <bookmark mark='a'/> To add a word, hash it once per row and add one to each of those counters. <bookmark mark='b'/> To estimate a word's count, look at the same d counters and take the smallest. <bookmark mark='c'/> Every counter holds the word's true count plus the counts of whatever other words collided with it there. Collisions only ever add, so the estimate is never too low, and the minimum picks the row with the fewest collisions.
bcc4efd81d7b.zh: Graham Cormode 与 S. Muthukrishnan 2005年的 Count-Min 草图保存一张小表：d 行，每行 w 个计数器，每行一个独立的哈希函数。<bookmark mark='a'/>要加入一个词，每行哈希一次，把那些计数器各加一。<bookmark mark='b'/>要估计一个词的计数，看同样的 d 个计数器，取最小值。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个计数器都等于这个词的真实计数，加上在那里与它碰撞的其他词的计数。碰撞只会增加，所以估计值从不偏低，而最小值选出了碰撞最少的那一行。

6dd1946f37d8.en: How large can the error be? <bookmark mark='a'/> In one row, the excess is the total count of the other words that hash to the same counter. With a good hash family, each other word lands there with probability one over w, so the expected excess is at most N over w, where N is the length of the stream. By Markov's inequality, the excess reaches e times that with probability at most one over e. <bookmark mark='b'/> The minimum is that bad only if every row is, and the rows are independent, so the probabilities multiply. <bookmark mark='c'/> Choose w as e over epsilon and d as log one over delta, and every estimate is within epsilon N of the truth with probability one minus delta. <bookmark mark='d'/> The memory depends on epsilon and delta, not on how many distinct words there are. <bookmark mark='e'/> On the novels, with four rows of 1021 counters, the guaranteed bound is about 12,273, no word came near it, and the typical excess was about 968. With two rows, a third of a percent of the words went over, well inside the thirteen and a half percent the theorem allows.
6dd1946f37d8.zh: 误差能有多大？<bookmark mark='a'/>在一行中，多出的部分是哈希到同一个计数器的其他词的总计数。用一个好的哈希族，每个其他词以 w 分之一的概率落在那里，所以期望的多余量至多为 N 除以 w，N 是数据流的长度。由马尔可夫不等式，多余量达到它的 e 倍的概率至多为 e 分之一。<bookmark mark='b'/>只有每一行都那么糟，最小值才会那么糟，而各行相互独立，所以概率相乘。<bookmark mark='c'/>取 w 为 e 除以 epsilon，d 为 log 一除以 delta，那么每个估计值以一减 delta 的概率落在真实值的 epsilon N 之内。<bookmark mark='d'/>内存取决于 epsilon 和 delta，与有多少个不同的词无关。<bookmark mark='e'/>在小说上，用四行、每行 1021 个计数器，保证的上界大约是 12273，没有一个词接近它，典型的多余量大约是 968。用两行时，百分之零点三的词超过了它，远在定理允许的百分之十三点五之内。

b7c777af3fb8.en: Chapter ten. The Job in kilobytes.
b7c777af3fb8.zh: 第10章。几千字节里的作业。

0d78a2a77d22.en: Now the Job itself, rebuilt so that it never stores the vocabulary. <bookmark mark='a'/> A Count-Min sketch of four rows of 1021 counters estimates every word's count. <bookmark mark='b'/> Only thirty-two words are kept, candidates for the top twenty, in a heap ordered by estimate; a word replaces the weakest when its estimate beats it. <bookmark mark='c'/> A table of a hundred and twenty-eight slots finds a word among the candidates, and an evicted one is deleted by shifting its neighbours back, Knuth's Algorithm R. <bookmark mark='d'/> Estan and Varghese's conservative update raises only the counters at the minimum: it still never undercounts, but it adds far less to other words. <bookmark mark='e'/> And double hashing gives all four row positions from one division per word.
0d78a2a77d22.zh: 现在是作业本身，重新构造成从不存储词汇表。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个四行、每行 1021 个计数器的 Count-Min 草图估计每个词的计数。<bookmark mark='b'/>只保留三十二个词，作为前二十名的候选，放在按估计值排序的堆里；一个词的估计值超过最弱的候选时就取代它。<bookmark mark='c'/>一张有一百二十八个槽的表在候选中查找一个词，被逐出的候选通过把邻居向后移动来删除，即 Knuth 的算法 R。<bookmark mark='d'/>Estan 与 Varghese 的保守更新只增加处于最小值的计数器：它仍然从不偏低，但给其他词增加的要少得多。<bookmark mark='e'/>而双重哈希每个词只用一次除法就给出全部四行的位置。

d03c09fc54f1.en: Here is the function that runs once per word, compiled by Part 13's compiler. <bookmark mark='a'/> First the four counter positions, each the last plus the step g, wrapped by a subtraction instead of a division. <bookmark mark='b'/> The estimate is the smallest of the four counters, <bookmark mark='c'/> and only the counters equal to it are raised. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then the test that makes the program cheap: if the heap is full and this word's estimate can't beat the weakest candidate, we are done. Almost every word in English stops here. <bookmark mark='e'/> A word that is already a candidate gets its new estimate and moves down the heap. <bookmark mark='f'/> Anything else joins, or replaces the weakest candidate.
d03c09fc54f1.zh: 这是每个词运行一次的函数，由第13部分的编译器编译。<bookmark mark='a'/>首先是四个计数器的位置，每个是前一个加上步长 g，用一次减法而不是除法来回绕。<bookmark mark='b'/>估计值是四个计数器中最小的，<bookmark mark='c'/>只有等于它的计数器才被增加。<bookmark mark='d'/>然后是让程序便宜的那个检验：如果堆已满，而这个词的估计值打不过最弱的候选，就结束。英语中几乎每个词都在这里停下。<bookmark mark='e'/>已经是候选的词得到新的估计值，在堆中下沉。<bookmark mark='f'/>其他的词加入，或者取代最弱的候选。

c8ce4f86f2d6.en: What does it remember? <bookmark mark='a'/> The sketch is sixteen thousand bytes. The candidates, their letters, the heap and the slots take about two thousand more. <bookmark mark='b'/> In all, 18,588 bytes, eighteen and a half kilobytes, in one block. <bookmark mark='c'/> Part 17's version kept every distinct word, almost fifty-eight thousand of them, with an entry and a slot each: 1.9 megabytes. <bookmark mark='d'/> A hundred times less. <bookmark mark='e'/> And eighteen and a half kilobytes fits in Part 9's level-one cache, so once the first few hundred words have touched every line, the program never misses again. We checked by tracing every load and store of a 150-kilobyte passage through the cache model: 295 lines in all, never more than 6 in a set of eight.
c8ce4f86f2d6.zh: 它记住了什么？<bookmark mark='a'/>草图是一万六千字节。候选、它们的字母、堆和槽另外大约占两千字节。<bookmark mark='b'/>一共 18588 字节，十八点五千字节，在一个连续的块中。<bookmark mark='c'/>第17部分的版本保存每个不同的词，将近五万八千个，每个一个条目和一个槽：1.9 兆字节。<bookmark mark='d'/>少了一百倍。<bookmark mark='e'/>而十八点五千字节装得进第9部分的一级缓存，所以一旦最初几百个词触及了每一行，程序就再也不会缺失。我们把一段 150 千字节的文本的每次读写都送进缓存模型来验证：一共 295 行，八路组中任何一组从未超过 6 行。

fb159065df6a.en: So the ledger gets its ninth row. Every one of the program's 1.1 billion instructions was run on the emulator, about 43 per byte of text, and the output matched the exact counts, word for word and digit for digit. <bookmark mark='a'/> Priced on Part 8's core: one second, a quarter slower than the hash table. <bookmark mark='b'/> The sketch does more work per word, and its chains of comparisons run fewer instructions per cycle. <bookmark mark='c'/> The hash table lost forty-four million cycles waiting for memory; the sketch, forty-six thousand. <bookmark mark='d'/> Row nine is not a speed-up. It buys memory: a hundred times less, for a quarter more time. That trade is the whole point of streaming algorithms, because for a real stream the vocabulary doesn't fit.
fb159065df6a.zh: 于是账本有了第九行。程序的 1.1 billion 条指令每一条都在模拟器上运行过，大约每字节文本 43 条，输出与精确计数逐词逐位一致。<bookmark mark='a'/>按第8部分的处理器计价：一秒，比哈希表慢四分之一。<bookmark mark='b'/>草图对每个词做的工作更多，它那一串比较每个周期执行的指令更少。<bookmark mark='c'/>哈希表有四千四百万个周期花在等待内存上；草图只有四万六千个。<bookmark mark='d'/>第九行不是一次提速。它买的是内存：少一百倍，多四分之一的时间。这种交换正是流算法的全部意义，因为对真实的数据流，词汇表是装不下的。

11bb5f9e4a4c.en: But was the exact answer luck? The hash function is the algorithm's coin, so we reran the same algorithm, in C, with twenty different hash functions, for several sketch sizes. <bookmark mark='a'/> With the program's own size, four rows of 1021 counters, the reported top twenty were exactly right, words and counts, for five of the twenty hash functions, and the program's own was one of the five. On average 19.1 of the twenty words were right, and never fewer than eighteen. <bookmark mark='b'/> The typical intruder is a rare word that collides with common ones in every row: vespasian, which appears in the novels once, was estimated at almost fifty-nine thousand. <bookmark mark='c'/> The plain update was never exact, and a sketch of two rows got only fourteen words right on average. Doubling the width to 32 kilobytes made seventy percent of the runs exact, and 64 kilobytes, ninety-five. <bookmark mark='d'/> This is a Monte Carlo algorithm: the memory and the time are guaranteed, the answer is probably right, and more memory buys more probability. <bookmark mark='e'/> And there is a cheap fix. In every one of the twenty runs, the true top twenty were among the thirty-two candidates. A second pass over the text, counting just those thirty-two words exactly, would have given the exact answer every time.
11bb5f9e4a4c.zh: 但这个精确的答案是运气吗？哈希函数就是算法的硬币，所以我们用 C 把同一个算法以二十个不同的哈希函数、在几种草图大小下重新运行。<bookmark mark='a'/>在程序自己的大小，即四行、每行 1021 个计数器时，报告的前二十名在二十个哈希函数中有五个完全正确，词和计数都对，而程序自己的那个就是这五个之一。平均二十个词中有 19.1 个正确，从未少于十八个。<bookmark mark='b'/>典型的闯入者是一个在每一行都与常用词碰撞的罕见词：vespasian，它在小说中出现一次，被估计为将近五万九千。<bookmark mark='c'/>普通更新从未完全正确，两行的草图平均只对了十四个词。把宽度加倍到 32 千字节，百分之七十的运行完全正确，64 千字节时是百分之九十五。<bookmark mark='d'/>这是一个蒙特卡洛算法：内存和时间是有保证的，答案很可能是对的，更多的内存换来更高的概率。<bookmark mark='e'/>还有一个便宜的修补办法。在二十次运行的每一次中，真正的前二十名都在三十二个候选之中。再扫描一遍文本，只精确统计这三十二个词，每次都会给出精确的答案。

fbb616459405.en: Chapter eleven. Counting distinct things: HyperLogLog.

117e332cc75b.en: How many different words are in the novels? Counting them exactly means remembering them all. <bookmark mark='a'/> Philippe Flajolet and Nigel Martin had a better idea in 1985. Hash each word to a string of random-looking bits, and look at how many zeros it starts with. A repeated word hashes the same way every time, so repeats change nothing. <bookmark mark='b'/> A hash that starts with rho minus one zeros and then a one has probability two to the minus rho. Seeing one is like flipping that many heads in a row: you need about two to the rho different items before it happens. <bookmark mark='c'/> So remember only the largest rank you have seen. That takes about log log n bits, five bits for any number of words you will ever meet. <bookmark mark='d'/> But a single record is noisy. One lucky hash, and the estimate doubles.
117e332cc75b.zh: 小说中有多少个不同的词？精确地数它们，意味着要记住所有的词。<bookmark mark='a'/>Philippe Flajolet 与 Nigel Martin 在1985年有一个更好的主意。把每个词哈希成一串看起来随机的比特，看它以多少个零开头。重复的词每次都哈希成同样的值，所以重复不改变任何东西。<bookmark mark='b'/>以 rho 减一个零开头、然后是一个一的哈希，概率是二的负 rho 次方。看到一个这样的哈希，就像连续抛出那么多次正面：在它出现之前，你大约需要二的 rho 次方个不同的数据项。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以只记住见过的最大秩。这大约需要 log log n 个比特，对你会遇到的任何数量的词都只要五个比特。<bookmark mark='d'/>但单个记录噪声很大。一个幸运的哈希，估计值就翻倍。

23d6905bce68.en: The cure is to average many records. <bookmark mark='a'/> Use the first few bits of each hash to choose one of m registers, and keep in each register the largest rank of the hashes sent to it. Here are sixty-four registers after the whole vocabulary of the novels. <bookmark mark='b'/> Philippe Flajolet and his colleagues combined them, in 2007, with a harmonic mean, which isn't fooled by a few lucky registers, times a constant that corrects the bias. <bookmark mark='c'/> The relative error is about one point zero four over the square root of m. <bookmark mark='d'/> When there are few items and many registers are still empty, it counts the empty ones instead.
23d6905bce68.zh: 解药是对许多记录取平均。<bookmark mark='a'/>用每个哈希的前几个比特选择 m 个寄存器之一，每个寄存器保存送到它那里的哈希的最大秩。这是处理完小说全部词汇后的六十四个寄存器。<bookmark mark='b'/>Philippe Flajolet 和他的同事在2007年用调和平均把它们组合起来，调和平均不会被少数幸运的寄存器骗到，再乘一个校正偏差的常数。<bookmark mark='c'/>相对误差大约是一点零四除以 m 的平方根。<bookmark mark='d'/>当数据项很少、许多寄存器还空着时，它改为数空寄存器的个数。

9eb769663172.en: We ran HyperLogLog on the novels' vocabulary with thirty different hash functions for each number of registers. <bookmark mark='a'/> The measured error follows one point zero four over root m down the table: sixteen registers, a quarter off; four thousand, one and a half percent, in three kilobytes. <bookmark mark='b'/> On the whole stream of four point six million words, the estimate was 58,012 against the true 57,895. <bookmark mark='c'/> And on every five-word phrase in the novels, four and a half million distinct ones, the same three kilobytes were off by half a percent. An exact count would need a table of tens of megabytes. <bookmark mark='d'/> This is why databases and analytics engines answer count distinct queries approximately, with HyperLogLog behind them.
9eb769663172.zh: 我们在小说的词汇上运行 HyperLogLog，对每种寄存器个数用三十个不同的哈希函数。<bookmark mark='a'/>测得的误差沿着表格向下遵循一点零四除以根号 m：十六个寄存器，偏差四分之一；四千个，百分之一点五，只用三千字节。<bookmark mark='b'/>在四百六十万个词的整个数据流上，估计值是 58012，真实值是 57895。<bookmark mark='c'/>而在小说中每一个五词短语上，四百五十万个不同的短语，同样的三千字节偏差为百分之零点五。精确计数需要一张几十兆字节的表。<bookmark mark='d'/>这就是为什么数据库和分析引擎近似地回答 count distinct 查询，背后是 HyperLogLog。

6b369d307dbf.en: Chapter twelve. Sketching the second moment.

a03a67f72116.en: Counting distinct items and counting the stream's length are two cases of one family. <bookmark mark='a'/> The p-th frequency moment is the sum, over items, of each item's count to the power p. <bookmark mark='b'/> F zero is the number of distinct items, the last chapter. <bookmark mark='c'/> F one is the length of the stream, which one counter tracks. <bookmark mark='d'/> F two, the sum of the squared counts, measures how concentrated the stream is. <bookmark mark='e'/> It is the number of rows when a database joins a table with itself on that column, and it jumps when a network sees a flood of identical packets. <bookmark mark='f'/> For the novels it is a hundred and seventy-seven billion, and the word the contributes thirty percent of it on its own. Can we estimate F two without counting every word?
a03a67f72116.zh: 统计不同的数据项和统计数据流的长度，是同一个家族的两个情形。<bookmark mark='a'/>第 p 阶频率矩是对所有数据项求和，每项是它的计数的 p 次方。<bookmark mark='b'/>F 零是不同数据项的个数，即上一章。<bookmark mark='c'/>F 一是数据流的长度，一个计数器就能跟踪。<bookmark mark='d'/>F 二是计数的平方和，衡量数据流有多集中。<bookmark mark='e'/>它是数据库在那一列上做表的自连接时的行数，当网络看到大量相同的数据包涌来时，它会猛增。<bookmark mark='f'/>对小说来说它是一千七百七十四亿，单是 the 这个词就贡献了百分之三十。能否不统计每个词就估计 F 二？

a827c8d1986c.en: Noga Alon, Yossi Matias and Mario Szegedy showed how in 1996, in the paper that started the theory of streaming. <bookmark mark='a'/> Give every item a random sign, plus or minus one, and keep a single number Z: each time an item arrives, add its sign. <bookmark mark='b'/> At the end, Z is the sum of each item's sign times its count. Square it. You get the squared counts, which is F two, plus cross terms, each a product of two different signs. <bookmark mark='c'/> Independent signs multiply to zero on average, so the expected value of Z squared is exactly F two. <bookmark mark='d'/> Its variance is at most twice F two squared, and that calculation needs only four-wise independent signs, which a small hash function supplies. <bookmark mark='e'/> Averaging k copies brings the relative error down to root two over k, and the median of a few such averages makes large errors exponentially unlikely. <bookmark mark='f'/> The median of means is a trick worth remembering: Chebyshev's inequality for each mean, a Chernoff bound for the median.
a827c8d1986c.zh: Noga Alon、Yossi Matias 与 Mario Szegedy 在1996年展示了做法，那篇论文开创了流算法的理论。<bookmark mark='a'/>给每个数据项一个随机符号，正一或负一，只保存一个数 Z：每当一个数据项到来，就加上它的符号。<bookmark mark='b'/>最后，Z 是每个数据项的符号乘它的计数之和。把它平方。你得到计数的平方，即 F 二，再加上交叉项，每个交叉项是两个不同符号的乘积。<bookmark mark='c'/>独立的符号相乘平均为零，所以 Z 平方的期望恰好是 F 二。<bookmark mark='d'/>它的方差至多是 F 二平方的两倍，而这个计算只需要四元独立的符号，一个小的哈希函数就能提供。<bookmark mark='e'/>对 k 个副本取平均，把相对误差降到根号下 k 分之二，再取几个这样的平均值的中位数，就让大的误差变得指数地不可能。<bookmark mark='f'/>均值的中位数是一个值得记住的技巧：对每个均值用切比雪夫不等式，对中位数用切尔诺夫界。

a46fa56c3c1b.en: On the novels. <bookmark mark='a'/> One copy of the sketch is wild: here are four hundred single estimates of F two, each divided by the truth. They scatter from nearly zero to several times too big, now and then ten times, but their average is right. <bookmark mark='b'/> Averaging k copies tightens them as predicted, about root two over k. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the median of nine averages cuts off the occasional bad average. With sixty-four copies in each of nine groups, the worst of forty trials was off by seventeen percent, from fewer than six hundred numbers. Each copy of Z is a dot product of the count vector with random signs, a random projection, the Johnson–Lindenstrauss idea from the AI series, and because it is linear, sketches of two streams simply add.
a46fa56c3c1b.zh: 在小说上。<bookmark mark='a'/>草图的单个副本很狂野：这是四百个 F 二的单次估计，各自除以真实值。它们从接近零分散到大好几倍，偶尔大十倍，但它们的平均值是对的。<bookmark mark='b'/>对 k 个副本取平均，正如预测的那样收紧，大约是根号下 k 分之二。<bookmark mark='c'/>九个平均值的中位数切掉了偶尔出现的坏平均值。每组六十四个副本、共九组时，四十次试验中最坏的一次偏差百分之十七，只用了不到六百个数。Z 的每个副本都是计数向量与随机符号的点积，即一次随机投影，也就是人工智能系列中的 Johnson–Lindenstrauss 思想；而且因为它是线性的，两个数据流的草图直接相加即可。

0de8fffd1aa9.en: Chapter thirteen. Near-duplicates: MinHash and locality-sensitive hashing.
0de8fffd1aa9.zh: 第13章。近似重复：MinHash 与局部敏感哈希。

8dc2b98a29b7.en: Search engines, plagiarism detectors and the people who clean training data for language models all need to find documents that are nearly the same. <bookmark mark='a'/> Represent a passage by its shingles, every run of five consecutive words. <bookmark mark='b'/> Two passages are as alike as the share of shingles they have in common: the Jaccard similarity, the size of the intersection over the size of the union. <bookmark mark='c'/> These two lines, from two versions of the same letter in The Count of Monte Cristo, share four of their ten distinct shingles, because changing one word breaks every shingle that contains it. <bookmark mark='d'/> The novels have thirty-four thousand paragraphs of forty words or more. Comparing every pair means almost six hundred million comparisons of sets.
8dc2b98a29b7.zh: 搜索引擎、抄袭检测器，以及为语言模型清洗训练数据的人，都需要找出几乎相同的文档。<bookmark mark='a'/>用瓦片来表示一段文字，即每一串连续的五个词。<bookmark mark='b'/>两段文字的相似程度，就是它们共有的瓦片所占的比例：杰卡德相似度，交集的大小除以并集的大小。<bookmark mark='c'/>这两行来自《基督山伯爵》中同一封信的两个版本，它们十个不同的瓦片中共有四个，因为改动一个词会破坏包含它的每一个瓦片。<bookmark mark='d'/>小说中有三万四千个四十词以上的段落。比较每一对，意味着将近六亿次集合比较。

0c182d012ab9.en: Andrei Broder found a shortcut in 1997, at the search engine AltaVista. <bookmark mark='a'/> Put every shingle in a random order, using a hash function, and look at the first shingle of the union of two sets. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each set's minimum hash is the same exactly when that first shingle belongs to both; here it is only in A, so they differ. By symmetry, every shingle of the union is equally likely to be first. <bookmark mark='c'/> So the two minimums agree with probability exactly the Jaccard similarity. <bookmark mark='d'/> Repeat with a hundred hash functions, and each paragraph becomes a signature of a hundred numbers. The share of positions where two signatures agree estimates their similarity, to within about five hundredths.
0c182d012ab9.zh: Andrei Broder 在1997年于搜索引擎 AltaVista 找到了一条捷径。<bookmark mark='a'/>用一个哈希函数把所有瓦片排成一个随机顺序，看两个集合并集中的第一个瓦片。<bookmark mark='b'/>两个集合的最小哈希相同，当且仅当这第一个瓦片同时属于两者；这里它只在 A 中，所以它们不同。由对称性，并集中每个瓦片成为第一个的可能性相同。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以两个最小值相同的概率恰好等于杰卡德相似度。<bookmark mark='d'/>用一百个哈希函数重复，每个段落就变成一个由一百个数组成的签名。两个签名一致的位置所占的比例估计它们的相似度，误差大约在百分之五以内。

d4a84fe5a65e.en: Signatures are short, but there are still six hundred million pairs of them. <bookmark mark='a'/> The last trick, locality-sensitive hashing, from Piotr Indyk and Rajeev Motwani, hashes the signatures themselves. Cut each into twenty bands of five numbers, and put each band into a hash table. <bookmark mark='b'/> Two paragraphs become candidates only if some band matches exactly. <bookmark mark='c'/> A band matches with probability J to the fifth, so the chance of becoming candidates is one minus one minus J to the fifth, to the twentieth. <bookmark mark='d'/> That curve is a step: pairs below a similarity of about a half are almost never compared, and pairs above seven tenths almost always are. We planted six hundred edited copies of paragraphs, and the share found at each similarity follows the curve.
d4a84fe5a65e.zh: 签名很短，但仍然有六亿对。<bookmark mark='a'/>最后一个技巧，Piotr Indyk 与 Rajeev Motwani 的局部敏感哈希，把签名本身再哈希一次。把每个签名切成二十段，每段五个数，把每一段放进一张哈希表。<bookmark mark='b'/>两个段落只有在某一段完全相同时才成为候选。<bookmark mark='c'/>一段相同的概率是 J 的五次方，所以成为候选的概率是一减去一减 J 的五次方的二十次方。<bookmark mark='d'/>这条曲线是一个台阶：相似度低于大约一半的对几乎从不被比较，高于十分之七的几乎总被比较。我们植入了六百个编辑过的段落副本，每种相似度下被找到的比例都沿着这条曲线。

6d46a1a55a61.en: Now the novels. <bookmark mark='a'/> Thirty-four thousand paragraphs, three and a half million shingles, six hundred million pairs. Computing every signature took two seconds, and the banding three more. It produced just 2 candidate pairs. <bookmark mark='b'/> To check, we found every pair of paragraphs that share even one uncommon shingle, with an inverted index, and computed their exact similarity. Only seven pairs in all thirty novels share a fifth of their phrases. <bookmark mark='c'/> The two above the threshold were both found: a table of contents in two editions, and the anonymous letter in The Count of Monte Cristo, which is quoted more than once, in different versions. The rest, a battle order repeated in War and Peace and a passage repeated in The Awakening, fall below the step, as the curve predicts. <bookmark mark='d'/> Novelists rarely repeat themselves; the Web does all the time. Google's crawler finds near-duplicate pages with a cousin of this idea, Moses Charikar's SimHash, and MinHash with banding is a standard step in cleaning the training data of language models.
6d46a1a55a61.zh: 现在看小说。<bookmark mark='a'/>三万四千个段落，三百五十万个瓦片，六亿对。计算全部签名用了两秒，分段又用了三秒。它只产生了 2 对候选。<bookmark mark='b'/>为了核对，我们用倒排索引找出了共有哪怕一个不常见瓦片的每一对段落，并计算了它们的精确相似度。全部三十部小说中，只有七对共享五分之一的短语。<bookmark mark='c'/>高于阈值的两对都被找到了：两个版本中的一份目录，以及《基督山伯爵》中那封匿名信，它被引用了不止一次，版本各不相同。其余的，《战争与和平》中重复的一道作战命令和《觉醒》中重复的一段，都落在台阶以下，正如曲线所预测的。<bookmark mark='d'/>小说家很少重复自己；网络却时时如此。谷歌的爬虫用这个想法的一个近亲，Moses Charikar 的 SimHash，来发现近似重复的网页，而带分段的 MinHash 是清洗语言模型训练数据的标准步骤。

9009f213a88f.en: Colour every edge of a complete graph red or blue. Frank Ramsey proved in 1930 that if the graph is big enough, some k vertices have all their edges the same colour, whatever you do. <bookmark mark='a'/> With four vertices, seventeen are not enough. On the left, a random colouring of the complete graph on seventeen vertices: on average it has 74 groups of four in a single colour. <bookmark mark='b'/> On the right, a clever colouring, blue exactly when the difference of the two vertices is a square modulo seventeen, has none at all. Eighteen vertices always contain one, so the Ramsey number R of four, four is eighteen. <bookmark mark='c'/> For five, nobody knows the answer: it is between forty-three and forty-six. For large k, clever colourings run out, but coins don't.
9009f213a88f.zh: 把一个完全图的每条边涂成红色或蓝色。Frank Ramsey 在1930年证明，只要图足够大，无论怎么涂，总有 k 个顶点之间的边全是同一种颜色。<bookmark mark='a'/>对四个顶点，十七个顶点是不够的。左边是十七个顶点的完全图的一个随机涂色：平均有 74 组四个顶点是单色的。<bookmark mark='b'/>右边是一个巧妙的涂色，当两个顶点之差是模十七的平方数时涂蓝色，它一组都没有。十八个顶点则总会有一组，所以拉姆齐数 R(4, 4) 是十八。<bookmark mark='c'/>对五，没有人知道答案：它在四十三和四十六之间。对大的 k，巧妙的涂色用完了，但硬币没有。

8dde4c360015.en: In 1947 Paul Erdős turned the question around. <bookmark mark='a'/> Colour each edge by a fair coin. A particular set of k vertices comes out all one colour with probability two times two to the minus k choose two. <bookmark mark='b'/> Add over all sets: if the expected number of one-colour sets is below one, then some colouring has none at all, because a random variable can't always be above its own average. <bookmark mark='c'/> The arithmetic works for n up to about two to the k over two. So the Ramsey number is at least that. <bookmark mark='d'/> Here is how far the count reaches for each k. The proof shows the colourings exist, and even that almost every colouring works, but it doesn't say how to write one down. <bookmark mark='e'/> Seventy-five years later, nobody can construct colourings anywhere near that good. <bookmark mark='f'/> The upper bound, four to the k, was improved for the first time in 2023, to four minus epsilon to the k, <bookmark mark='g'/> while the lower bound from coins has barely moved since 1947.
8dde4c360015.zh: 1947年，Paul Erdős 把问题反过来问。<bookmark mark='a'/>用一枚公平的硬币给每条边涂色。一组特定的 k 个顶点全部同色的概率是二乘二的负 k 选二次方。<bookmark mark='b'/>对所有的组求和：如果单色组的期望个数小于一，那么一定有某种涂色一组都没有，因为一个随机变量不可能总是高于它自己的平均值。<bookmark mark='c'/>这个算术对 n 直到大约二的 k 除以二次方都成立。所以拉姆齐数至少是这么多。<bookmark mark='d'/>这是对每个 k，计数能达到多远。证明表明这样的涂色存在，甚至几乎每一种涂色都可以，但它没有告诉我们怎样写下一个。<bookmark mark='e'/>七十五年后，仍没有人能构造出接近这么好的涂色。<bookmark mark='f'/>上界四的 k 次方在2023年第一次被改进，改为四减 epsilon 的 k 次方，<bookmark mark='g'/>而来自硬币的下界自1947年以来几乎没有动过。

4885a95eaf75.en: Sometimes the good outcome is very unlikely, and counting fails. <bookmark mark='a'/> Suppose there are many bad events, each of small probability p, and each one independent of all but d of the others. <bookmark mark='b'/> If e times p times d plus one is at most one, then with positive probability none of them happens. <bookmark mark='c'/> That is the Lovász local lemma, from Erdős and Lovász in 1975. The probability can be exponentially small, but it isn't zero, so the good outcome exists. <bookmark mark='d'/> For example, a k-SAT formula in which every clause shares variables with fewer than about two to the k over e others is always satisfiable. <bookmark mark='e'/> For thirty-five years the proof gave no way to find the assignment. Then in 2010 Robin Moser and Gábor Tardos showed that the most naive algorithm works: while some clause is false, give its variables fresh random values. <bookmark mark='f'/> We built 10-SAT formulas where each clause meets about three hundred others, inside the lemma's condition. Each needed only about as many resamplings as it had false clauses at the start, far inside the bound of m over d.
4885a95eaf75.zh: 有时好的结果非常不可能出现，计数就失效了。<bookmark mark='a'/>假设有许多坏事件，每个的概率都很小，为 p，并且每个只与其余事件中的 d 个不独立。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果 e 乘 p 乘 d 加一至多为一，那么以正的概率它们一个都不发生。<bookmark mark='c'/>这就是 Erdős 与 Lovász 1975年的洛瓦兹局部引理。概率可以指数地小，但它不是零，所以好的结果存在。<bookmark mark='d'/>例如，一个 k-SAT 公式，如果每个子句与少于大约二的 k 次方除以 e 个其他子句共享变量，它总是可满足的。<bookmark mark='e'/>三十五年来，这个证明没有给出找到赋值的办法。然后在2010年，Robin Moser 与 Gábor Tardos 证明最朴素的算法就行：只要有子句为假，就给它的变量新的随机值。<bookmark mark='f'/>我们构造了一些 10-SAT 公式，每个子句与大约三百个其他子句相交，在引理的条件之内。每个公式需要的重新抽样次数，大约只和开始时为假的子句数一样多，远在 m 除以 d 的上界之内。

b5d18c460bc0.en: Chapter fifteen. Removing the coins, and where they come from.
b5d18c460bc0.zh: 第15章。去掉硬币，以及硬币从哪里来。

1d498504c250.en: Can the coins be removed? Sometimes, mechanically. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take MAX-CUT: split the vertices of a graph into two sides so that as many edges as possible cross. It is NP-hard, as Part 26 will show. <bookmark mark='b'/> A random split cuts each edge with probability a half, so on average it cuts half of them. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now place the vertices one at a time, and put each on the side that cuts more edges to the vertices already placed. <bookmark mark='d'/> At every step, the expected cut, given the choices so far, is the average of the two possible choices, so the better choice can't be below it. It starts at m over two and never falls, so the final cut, which is no longer random, is at least m over two. <bookmark mark='e'/> On a random graph with two hundred and sixty-five edges, random splits averaged half, and the best of two thousand cut one hundred and sixty-two. The deterministic walk through the expectations cut one hundred and seventy-six.
1d498504c250.zh: 硬币能去掉吗？有时可以，而且是机械地。<bookmark mark='a'/>看最大割：把图的顶点分成两边，使跨越两边的边尽可能多。它是 NP 难的，第26部分会证明。<bookmark mark='b'/>随机分割以二分之一的概率切断每条边，所以平均切断一半。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在一次放置一个顶点，把每个顶点放在与已放置的顶点之间切断更多边的那一边。<bookmark mark='d'/>每一步，在已有选择下的期望割，是两种可能选择的平均，所以较好的选择不会低于它。它从 m 除以二开始，从不下降，所以最终的割，已不再随机，至少是 m 除以二。<bookmark mark='e'/>在一个有二百六十五条边的随机图上，随机分割平均切断一半，两千次中最好的切断了一百六十二条。沿着期望确定性地走下来，切断了一百七十六条。

b1823d30465f.en: There is a second way. <bookmark mark='a'/> The MAX-CUT argument looks at one edge at a time, which involves only two vertices' coins. <bookmark mark='b'/> So the coins don't need to be fully independent, only pairwise independent. <bookmark mark='c'/> Pairwise independent bits are cheap. Pick k truly random bits s, and give vertex i the parity of the bits of s where i's binary expansion has a one. <bookmark mark='d'/> Any two of these bits are independent and fair, so k coins become about two to the k. <bookmark mark='e'/> With only about n possible seeds, we can try every one, deterministically, and keep the best cut: the expectation guarantees one of them reaches m over two. <bookmark mark='f'/> Limited independence, small-bias spaces and walks on expander graphs, Part 56, are the general tools for stretching a few random bits a long way.
b1823d30465f.zh: 还有第二种办法。<bookmark mark='a'/>最大割的论证一次只看一条边，只涉及两个顶点的硬币。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以硬币不必完全独立，只需两两独立。<bookmark mark='c'/>两两独立的比特很便宜。取 k 个真正随机的比特 s，让顶点 i 取 s 在 i 的二进制展开为一的那些位上的奇偶性。<bookmark mark='d'/>任意两个这样的比特都是独立且公平的，所以 k 枚硬币变成了大约二的 k 次方枚。<bookmark mark='e'/>可能的种子只有大约 n 个，我们可以确定性地试遍每一个，保留最好的割：期望保证其中有一个达到 m 除以二。<bookmark mark='f'/>有限独立性、小偏差空间和扩展图上的游走，第56部分，是把少量随机比特拉长使用的一般工具。

5e27cc24d495.en: Every algorithm in this part assumed fair, independent coins. Computers usually have none, and use pseudorandom generators instead. <bookmark mark='a'/> In the 1960s and 70s, many scientific programs used IBM's RANDU: multiply by sixty-five thousand five hundred and thirty-nine, modulo two to the thirty-one. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here are two and a half thousand consecutive triples of its outputs, plotted as points in a cube. They look random. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now turn the cube. <bookmark mark='d'/> The multiplier is two to the sixteen plus three, and squaring it shows that each output is six times the previous one minus nine times the one before, modulo two to the thirty-one. <bookmark mark='e'/> So nine u minus six v plus w is always a whole number, and every point lies on one of just 15 planes. Any simulation that sampled points in space with RANDU was sampling fifteen sheets. Donald Knuth called it truly horrible.
5e27cc24d495.zh: 这一部分的每个算法都假定有公平、独立的硬币。计算机通常没有，而是用伪随机数生成器代替。<bookmark mark='a'/>在二十世纪六七十年代，许多科学程序使用 IBM 的 RANDU：乘以六万五千五百三十九，再模二的三十一次方。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是它连续输出的两千五百个三元组，画成立方体中的点。它们看起来是随机的。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在转动立方体。<bookmark mark='d'/>乘数是二的十六次方加三，把它平方可以看出，每个输出等于前一个的六倍减去再前一个的九倍，模二的三十一次方。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以九 u 减六 v 加 w 总是整数，每个点都落在仅仅 15 个平面之一上。任何用 RANDU 在空间中取样的模拟，取样的都只是十五张薄片。Donald Knuth 称它真正可怕。

8ef54c499b3c.en: Modern generators are far better. <bookmark mark='a'/> The Mersenne Twister, from 1998, behind Python's random module, passes the usual statistical tests, but it is linear: six hundred and twenty-four outputs reveal every future one. Fine for simulations, useless for secrets. <bookmark mark='b'/> PCG and xoshiro are smaller and faster; numpy uses PCG. <bookmark mark='c'/> Cryptographic generators such as ChaCha20 are designed so that no efficient test can tell them from coins, if the cipher is secure; Part 29 builds them. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the seed comes from physical noise, pooled by the operating system.
8ef54c499b3c.zh: 现代的生成器好得多。<bookmark mark='a'/>1998年的梅森旋转算法是 Python random 模块背后的算法，能通过常见的统计检验，但它是线性的：六百二十四个输出就暴露了以后的每一个输出。用于模拟没问题，用于保密毫无用处。<bookmark mark='b'/>PCG 和 xoshiro 更小、更快；numpy 用的是 PCG。<bookmark mark='c'/>ChaCha20 这样的密码学生成器的设计目标是：只要密码是安全的，任何高效的检验都无法把它们与硬币区分开；第29部分会构造它们。<bookmark mark='d'/>而种子来自物理噪声，由操作系统汇集起来。

c62755fe4ca4.en: Chapter sixteen. Frontier: does randomness help?
c62755fe4ca4.zh: 第16章。前沿：随机性有用吗？

84ed7b96fb50.en: Many of this part's coins have since been removed, one problem at a time. <bookmark mark='a'/> Primality got a deterministic polynomial test in 2002; logarithmic-space connectivity lost its random walk in 2005; near-linear minimum cuts became deterministic in 2015 and, for weighted graphs, in 2024; and in 2016 Fenner, Gurjar and Thierauf nearly removed the coins from parallel bipartite matching. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each took years and its own idea. Is there a general reason this keeps working?
84ed7b96fb50.zh: 这一部分的许多硬币后来都被去掉了，一次一个问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>素性检验在2002年有了确定性的多项式检验；对数空间的连通性检验在2005年去掉了随机游走；近线性时间的最小割在2015年、对带权图在2024年成为确定性的；2016年，Fenner、Gurjar 与 Thierauf 几乎去掉了并行二部图匹配中的硬币。<bookmark mark='b'/>每一项都花了多年，各需要自己的想法。这一再成功，背后有没有一般的原因？

9677096e683d.en: There is, conditionally. <bookmark mark='a'/> Call BPP the problems that a polynomial-time algorithm with coins solves with error at most a third. <bookmark mark='b'/> Suppose we had a pseudorandom generator that stretched a logarithmic number of truly random bits into n bits that no small circuit can tell from coins. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then we could try every seed, only polynomially many, and take the majority answer. No coins at all. <bookmark mark='d'/> Noam Nisan and Avi Wigderson, and then Russell Impagliazzo and Wigderson, showed how to build such a generator from any sufficiently hard function. <bookmark mark='e'/> If some problem solvable in exponential time needs exponentially large circuits, then P equals BPP: every randomized algorithm can be derandomized with polynomial slowdown. <bookmark mark='f'/> Hard functions make good coins. Most complexity theorists believe P equals BPP, and Part 27 follows the argument further.
9677096e683d.zh: 有，在一定条件下。<bookmark mark='a'/>把 BPP 称为：用硬币的多项式时间算法能以至多三分之一的错误解决的问题。<bookmark mark='b'/>假设我们有一个伪随机数生成器，能把对数个真正随机的比特拉长成 n 个比特，任何小电路都无法把它们与硬币区分开。<bookmark mark='c'/>那么我们就可以试遍每一个种子，只有多项式多个，再取多数答案。完全不用硬币。<bookmark mark='d'/>Noam Nisan 与 Avi Wigderson，随后 Russell Impagliazzo 与 Wigderson，展示了怎样从任何足够难的函数构造这样的生成器。<bookmark mark='e'/>如果某个能在指数时间内解决的问题需要指数大的电路，那么 P 等于 BPP：每个随机算法都能以多项式的减速去随机化。<bookmark mark='f'/>难的函数造出好的硬币。大多数复杂性理论学者相信 P 等于 BPP，第27部分会把这个论证进一步展开。

6d8812971451.en: And the converse holds too, which is why the question is so hard. <bookmark mark='a'/> Polynomial identity testing asks whether an arithmetic circuit computes the zero polynomial. <bookmark mark='b'/> With coins it is easy: evaluate at one random point, chapter three. <bookmark mark='c'/> Without coins, no polynomial-time algorithm is known. <bookmark mark='d'/> Valentine Kabanets and Russell Impagliazzo proved in 2004 that a deterministic algorithm would itself prove a circuit lower bound of a kind complexity theory has sought for fifty years. <bookmark mark='e'/> So removing this one coin is as hard as the great open problems of lower bounds. <bookmark mark='f'/> Special cases are solved, such as sparse polynomials and some restricted kinds of circuit, and the matching result of 2016 came from this line of work.
6d8812971451.zh: 而反方向也成立，这就是这个问题如此困难的原因。<bookmark mark='a'/>多项式恒等式检验问：一个算术电路计算的是否是零多项式。<bookmark mark='b'/>有硬币时它很容易：在一个随机点上求值，第3章。<bookmark mark='c'/>没有硬币时，不知道任何多项式时间算法。<bookmark mark='d'/>Valentine Kabanets 与 Russell Impagliazzo 在2004年证明，一个确定性算法本身就会证明一种电路下界，而那种下界复杂性理论已经追寻了五十年。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以去掉这一枚硬币，与下界方面的重大未解问题一样难。<bookmark mark='f'/>一些特殊情形已经解决，比如稀疏多项式和某些受限的电路，2016年的匹配结果也来自这一研究方向。

184980fa13cd.en: For sketches, the theory is unusually complete. <bookmark mark='a'/> Counting distinct items to within one plus or minus epsilon needs about one over epsilon squared bits, plus log n, and in 2010 Daniel Kane, Jelani Nelson and David Woodruff matched that exactly. The second moment is similar. For higher moments, a polynomial amount of space is provably necessary. Count-Min is close to optimal for estimating single counts, and finding the exact top words in small space is impossible: the Job's sketch must sometimes be wrong. <bookmark mark='b'/> The lower bounds come from communication complexity. If a small sketch existed, two people could pass it between them and solve a problem that provably needs a long conversation. Part 27 proves those.
184980fa13cd.zh: 对于草图，理论异常完整。<bookmark mark='a'/>把不同数据项的个数统计到一加减 epsilon 以内，需要大约一除以 epsilon 平方个比特，再加 log n，2010年 Daniel Kane、Jelani Nelson 与 David Woodruff 恰好达到了它。二阶矩类似。对更高阶的矩，多项式大小的空间被证明是必需的。Count-Min 在估计单个计数上接近最优，而在小空间里找出精确的前几名是不可能的：作业的草图必定有时会出错。<bookmark mark='b'/>下界来自通信复杂性。如果存在一个小草图，两个人就可以互相传递它，解决一个被证明需要长时间交谈的问题。第27部分会证明这些。

9e9b4163d6a3.en: Here is where things stand. <bookmark mark='a'/> Does P equal BPP, and can that be proved without first proving circuit lower bounds? <bookmark mark='b'/> Is there a deterministic polynomial-time test for polynomial identities? <bookmark mark='c'/> Can anyone write down a colouring of a complete graph that is as good as a random one? Explicit constructions improved dramatically after 2016, with two-source extractors, but still fall short. <bookmark mark='d'/> And can perfect matchings be found fast in parallel without coins, for every graph? <bookmark mark='e'/> This part's research problem takes the second.
9e9b4163d6a3.zh: 这就是现状。<bookmark mark='a'/>P 等于 BPP 吗？能否不先证明电路下界就证明它？<bookmark mark='b'/>多项式恒等式有没有确定性的多项式时间检验？<bookmark mark='c'/>有没有人能写下一个完全图的涂色，和随机涂色一样好？2016年以后，借助双源提取器，显式构造有了巨大的进步，但仍有差距。<bookmark mark='d'/>能否不用硬币，对每个图都在并行中快速找到完美匹配？<bookmark mark='e'/>这一部分的研究题处理的是第二个。

2676cb41f9f5.en: What we built in this part. Las Vegas and Monte Carlo, and amplification. Freivalds' check and the Schwartz–Zippel lemma, with perfect matchings and fingerprints. Karger's random contractions. Miller–Rabin. Random walks for satisfiability, balls in bins and the power of two choices. Bloom filters, reservoirs, Misra–Gries and Count-Min, and the Job in eighteen kilobytes. HyperLogLog, the AMS sketch and MinHash. The probabilistic method, and the ways to remove the coins.
2676cb41f9f5.zh: 这一部分我们造了什么。拉斯维加斯与蒙特卡洛，以及放大。Freivalds 的检验和 Schwartz–Zippel 引理，以及完美匹配和指纹。Karger 的随机收缩。Miller–Rabin。求解可满足性的随机游走，球与箱，以及两个选择的力量。布隆过滤器、蓄水池、Misra–Gries 和 Count-Min，以及十八千字节里的作业。HyperLogLog、AMS 草图和 MinHash。概率方法，以及去掉硬币的办法。

d963294d6de3.en: Where this comes back. Part 21 turns fingerprints into Rabin and Karp's string search, and Part 22 uses locality-sensitive hashing for nearest neighbours. Part 23 rounds linear programs at random, including MAX-CUT's famous 0.878. Part 27 develops BPP, hardness against randomness and the lower bounds for streams. Part 29 builds cryptographic generators, and Part 30 needs the big primes. Part 34's storage engines keep a Bloom filter per file; Parts 46 and 47 run sketches and SimHash in production; and Part 48's load balancers use two choices, while Part 56 builds the expanders.
d963294d6de3.zh: 这些会在哪里再出现。第21部分把指纹变成 Rabin 与 Karp 的字符串搜索，第22部分用局部敏感哈希寻找最近邻。第23部分随机地舍入线性规划，包括最大割著名的 0.878。第27部分发展 BPP、硬度与随机性，以及数据流的下界。第29部分构造密码学生成器，第30部分需要大素数。第34部分的存储引擎为每个文件保存一个布隆过滤器；第46和47部分在生产中运行草图和 SimHash；第48部分的负载均衡器使用两个选择，而第56部分构造扩展图。

2ebe940ce8ae.en: In practice. Databases put Bloom filters in front of their files and answer count-distinct queries with HyperLogLog. Routers track heavy hitters with sketches, and load balancers pick the less busy of two servers. Modern caches decide what to keep with a Count-Min filter. Web crawls and the training sets of language models are deduplicated with MinHash. And every secure connection begins with random primes and a cryptographic generator.
2ebe940ce8ae.zh: 在实践中。数据库在文件前面放布隆过滤器，用 HyperLogLog 回答 count distinct 查询。路由器用草图跟踪频繁项，负载均衡器在两台服务器中挑较闲的那台。现代缓存用一个 Count-Min 过滤器决定保留什么。网络爬取的数据和语言模型的训练集用 MinHash 去重。而每一次安全连接都从随机素数和一个密码学生成器开始。

ef001bc3cdce.en: Six problems, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: HyperLogLog in the Pebble language, which has no bitwise operators, so the ranks come from repeated halving. The last, marked with a star, is a research problem: its answer is not known, and the notes say where to start.
ef001bc3cdce.zh: 六道习题，完整的解答在这一部分的讲义里。在任何一道上都可以暂停。第五道是动手题：用 Pebble 语言实现 HyperLogLog，这门语言没有位运算，所以秩要靠反复折半得到。最后一道标着星号，是研究题：它的答案还不知道，讲义里说了从哪里开始。

b7f61567a7f2.en: Next time, the oldest data of all, text. Searching it efficiently leads to automata built from patterns, to indexes of every suffix, and to a reversible transform that sorts a book into compressible runs, so that we can search the novels while they stay compressed. And every git diff turns out to be a shortest path on a grid. Part 21, Strings.
b7f61567a7f2.zh: 下一次，最古老的数据：文本。高效地搜索它，引出了由模式构造的自动机、所有后缀的索引，以及一种把一本书排成可压缩的字符串的可逆变换，让我们可以在小说保持压缩的状态下搜索它们。而每一次 git diff 原来都是网格上的一条最短路径。第21部分，字符串。

9bd24692775d.en: The books and papers this part follows are on screen and in the notes. Thank you for watching.
9bd24692775d.zh: 这一部分所依据的书和论文都在屏幕上，也在讲义里。感谢收看。
